deals.notes: LaGrange Marketplace is a 76,594 SF Food Depot-anchored neighborhood center at the SR-29 / Youngs Mill Road intersection (21,110 VPD) in LaGrange, Georgia, one mile from downtown and 2.5 miles from I-85, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. The center is 87.1% leased and generates $424,760 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $632,559 of effective gross revenue against $207,799 of operating expenses — a $5.55/SF NOI that reflects both the low rent basis and the 13% vacancy. Food Depot, an employee-owned regional grocer with 40+ Georgia stores, has operated here since 2008, extended for ten years in 2018, and occupies 61% of the GLA at just $3.25/SF, which is 34% of base rent and 43% of total revenue. That rent is far below market and therefore very sticky income, but it is locked by options running to April 2038 and cannot be marked to market inside a normal hold — and the OM discloses no store sales, so the anchor's health is untested even though its primary term expires in April 2028. Grocery competition in the trade area is fully defined and long-established, with Publix, Kroger and a Walmart Neighborhood Market all within one mile and each in place for 11+ years, which the broker frames as evidence Food Depot has carved out a durable value niche. The investment case is the 9,894 SF of vacancy across four shop suites plus a demonstrated 20% average rent spread on the two most recent renewals, together driving CBRE's 7.62% five-year NOI CAGR. The trade area is the weakest in this portfolio group — $75,444 3-mile average household income and $54,635 median — which argues for cap-rate cushion rather than aggressive rent growth, notwithstanding 1.3% annual population growth and several hundred new homes and apartments under construction nearby. The top risk is unambiguous: a single below-market grocer with no disclosed sales carries nearly half the revenue and reaches a term decision within eighteen months.

deals.notes: Parkway Plaza is a 52,365 SF Aldi-anchored neighborhood center at the signalized Perry Lane Road / Golden Isles Parkway intersection (33,600 VPD) in Brunswick, Georgia, half a mile from the I-95 interchange, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. Aldi converted the former Winn-Dixie box — in place at this location since 2002 — and opened in December 2024, taking 37,985 SF at $9.64/SF stepping to $10.86/SF in October 2027, with roughly eight years of primary term to December 2034. That single tenant is 73% of the GLA, 75% of base rent and 76% of revenue, so the asset underwrites much closer to a net-leased grocery box with a four-suite shop strip attached than to a diversified center. In-place CY2027 NOI is $460,765 on $637,885 of effective gross revenue against $177,120 of operating expenses, with a $11.23/SF weighted-average base rent. The most important term in the deal is buried in a rent-roll footnote: Aldi occupies only about 60% of its premises but pays rent on all of it, and after March 2027 the landlord may recapture the remaining ~40% on thirty days' notice if Aldi has not subleased it — at which point Aldi's rent and recoveries would apply only to the space it occupies. CBRE models no recapture and never discloses the resulting rent, so a meaningful share of the anchor's income is unresolved until the lease is read. The growth case is the 7,980 SF vacancy (a single large-shop block, not easy small-shop fill) plus a speculative ground lease on the included ±2.09-acre outparcel at $125,000/year from year four, which is the entire difference between CBRE's 9% and 12.8% five-year NOI CAGR. The trade area is genuinely good — $104,045 3-mile average household income, $117,986 within a mile, 2.78% annual 1-mile population growth and 186 new apartments a mile north — and grocery competition is unusually thin, with the nearest store two miles away. The top risk is that no sales are disclosed for any tenant, Aldi included, so an asset whose value is three-quarters one lease offers no way to test that lease's health.

NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — this is an unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $615,795 in-place NOI.

Expenses are CBRE's model of the 2026 budget, with non-recoverable ownership-specific expenses stripped out and replaced by a $0.05/SF assumption. Reimbursements toward amortized deferred capital projects are modeled BELOW the NOI line, so the recovery figure here excludes them.

redFlags.description: Cato is the center's clear problem tenant: $79 PSF of sales against a 21.32% occupancy cost (OM-stated) on 6,080 SF, expiring 01/31/2028 with NO remaining renewal options. The OM presents Cato among its below-market mark-to-market opportunities; the sales data says the opposite — this is a renewal/vacancy risk on 11% of GLA, not upside.

39% of GLA (Planet Fitness, 20,955 SF) rolls in a single year, 08/03/2032, and it is the only in-line anchor. There is no disclosed renewal option and no co-tenancy protection. A Planet Fitness non-renewal is the single largest swing factor in the hold.

The real anchor is NOT owned. Kroger sits on the NAP parcel and drives the 1M+ annual visits the whole investment thesis rests on, but ownership has no lease, no term, and no go-dark protection over it — only a $2,472/yr shared-utility contribution. A Kroger closure or relocation would hit in-line rents with nothing to offset it.

Near-term rollover is heavy and largely unprotected: KORT Physical Therapy (5,000 SF, 11/30/2027), New York Fashions (3,060 SF, 12/31/2027), Cato (6,080 SF, 01/31/2028), Nails Pro (900 SF, 03/31/2028) and China King (1,050 SF, 05/31/2028) — 16,090 SF / 29.6% of GLA — expire within roughly 18 months of the CY2027 analysis start, and the OM says four of them have no remaining options. CBRE's in-place NOI assumes they simply stay at current rents, so the $615,795 carries no downtime or re-leasing cost for any of it.

Taxes are NOT reassessed in the pro-forma. Kentucky assesses at fair cash value annually; a purchase will very likely reset the assessment, and the $88,475 modeled tax line is 14% of NOI — a meaningful post-close step-up risk the pro-forma does not carry.

Cato's 5% NON-CUMULATIVE cap on CAM, taxes AND insurance caps recovery growth on 11% of GLA. Because it covers taxes as well as CAM, it also blunts the recovery of any post-sale tax reassessment on that suite.
Sales data is disclosed for only two of the ten in-line tenants (Shoe Station and Cato). Occupancy cost and tenant health are unknown for the rest of the roster, including Planet Fitness.

deals.notes: Bryan Station is a 54,277 SF neighborhood shopping center on Bryan Station Road in northeast Lexington, Kentucky, offered unpriced by CBRE as part of the Project Evergreen portfolio. The asset's traffic thesis rests on a Kroger that generates over 1 million annual visits — but that Kroger sits on the adjacent NAP parcel and is NOT part of the offering, so ownership carries none of the lease control that normally underpins a grocery-anchored center. The owned rent roll is 94.5% leased at a $12.55/SF weighted-average base rent against CBRE's $14.34/SF modeled market rent, producing $615,795 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $888,433 of effective gross revenue and $272,638 of operating expenses. Planet Fitness is the only in-line anchor at 20,955 SF (38.6% of GLA) and pays just $8.41/SF through August 2032, which is real mark-to-market depth but also concentrates 39% of the center's area in one uncontracted 2032 expiry. The near-term picture is busier than the headline suggests: KORT Physical Therapy, New York Fashions, Cato, Nails Pro and China King — 16,090 SF, 29.6% of GLA — all expire between November 2027 and May 2028, and CBRE's in-place NOI simply assumes they hold over at current rents with no downtime or re-leasing cost. Cato is the tenant to underwrite hardest: $79 PSF of sales against a 21.32% occupancy cost on 6,080 SF expiring January 2028 with no options is a vacancy risk, notwithstanding the OM's framing of it as below-market upside. The investment case is a 4.08% modeled 10-year NOI CAGR from lease-up of the single 3,002 SF vacancy plus mark-to-market on Planet Fitness and Pizza Hut, into a trade area with a $97,726 3-mile average household income growing 16% over five years. The top risk is structural rather than operational — an un-owned grocery anchor and a single 39%-of-GLA fitness tenant carry the traffic and the income, and neither is protected by anything in the deal.

FOOTNOTE RECONSTRUCTION — IMPORTANT. The OM's page-9 footnote block extracts OUT OF ORDER, so the numbered markers had to be re-tied to tenants rather than read straight off. Every assignment used here is confirmed ARITHMETICALLY, not guessed: the four pending-renewal notes reproduce the exact CY2027 blended PSF for Omelet Cafe ($23.30 x 8mo + $24.50 x 4mo = $23.70), Sally Beauty ($21.78 x 3mo + $24.50 x 9mo = $23.82), Sport Clips ($21.78 x 8mo + $24.50 x 4mo = $22.69) and GameStop ($22.00 x 1mo + $24.50 x 11mo = $24.29); the 7%-over-$775,000 percentage rent ties to Kobe (the only tenant with percentage rent, and the only December 2031 expiry); the 12%-over-$583,333 note ties to Cato ($583,333 x 12% = $70,000, the natural breakpoint on Cato's $69,993 base rent); the May 2027 - April 2028 '6th lease year' kickout ties to Petsense (commenced April/May 2022); leaving the February 2027 - January 2028 $2M kickout with Bealls Outlet, whose fiscal year ends in January and whose $2M threshold is ~$86/SF on 23,275 SF. Spot-check these against the rent roll, but each one reproduces a printed figure exactly.

FOUR OF THE NINETEEN LEASES ARE ON PENDING, UNEXECUTED RENEWALS that CBRE has modeled (Omelet Cafe, Sally Beauty, Sport Clips, GameStop — all marked with an asterisk on the site plan). Their contractual leases expire in March 2027, August 2027 (x2) and January 2027. The site plan's own footnote says the expirations 'reflect pending lease extension.' Together that is 25% of the GLA recovering nothing, which points to gross or heavily capped structures and is why the center recovers only $204,109 against $304,610 of operating expenses (a 67% recovery ratio). Verify both structures against the leases.

The CVS and AutoZone REA rows print an impossible date range in the OM (Start Jan-23, End Dec-21). Those dates are LEFT NULL here rather than carried into the library; both rows are marked NAP so they do not distort GLA, occupancy or rent-PSF math, and their $4,619 of combined CAM contribution remains inside the $204,109 recovery line.

Bealls Outlet, the largest tenant at 20.5% of GLA, has a one-time kickout if February 2027 - January 2028 sales are under $2,000,000; Petsense has a one-time kickout after its 6th lease year (May 2027 - April 2028) if sales do not exceed $700,000. Get the sales before bidding.

25% of the GLA recovers nothing. Bealls Outlet (23,275 SF) and Cato (4,950 SF) are both modeled with $0 expense reimbursement, which is why the center recovers only $204,109 against $304,610 of operating expenses — a 67% recovery ratio that is weak for a center marketed as NNN. Every dollar of expense growth on those two suites, including a post-sale tax reassessment, falls to ownership.

The modeled real-estate tax line is $74,129, just $0.65/SF on a 113,652 SF center — implausibly low for a Georgia community center at a major intersection, and expressly NOT reassessed. A reassessment to a market purchase price could move this line materially, and 25% of the GLA cannot recover any of it.

Cato is a watch item: $110 PSF of sales at a 13% occupancy cost (OM-stated), expiring January 2028, with sales BELOW its $583,333 percentage-rent breakpoint so it generates no overage. Shoe Show is worse on health — a 14% occupancy cost on $139 PSF — and expires October 2027, the very first roll.
GameStop's modeled renewal is only TWO YEARS, versus five for the other three pending renewals — a signal about that tenant's own commitment in a business that is closing stores nationally.

SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ONLY FOUR OF NINETEEN TENANTS (Kobe, Cato, Hibbett, Shoe Show). The three largest tenants by area — Bealls Outlet, Harbor Freight and Goodwill, 57% of GLA between them — have no productivity data at all, and two of the four disclosed tenants are the weakest performers.

deals.notes: Fort Howard Square is a 113,652 SF, 100% leased community center on 12.7 acres at the South Columbia Avenue / Fort Howard Road intersection (34,800 VPD) in Rincon, Georgia, a fast-growing Savannah suburb, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is the dominant center in its trade area — #1 of four within five miles by foot traffic with 71% more visits than the runner-up, 1.7 million annual visits, and the next comparable retail concentration 10+ miles away — anchored by Bealls Outlet, Harbor Freight, Goodwill and Dollar Tree and drawing cross-shopping from a Walmart Supercenter, Lowe's and Kroger Marketplace at the same corner. In-place CY2027 NOI is $1,290,174 on $1,594,783 of effective gross revenue against $304,610 of operating expenses, at a roster-computed $11.96/SF weighted-average base rent against CBRE's $16.17/SF modeled market rent — the 24%-below-market spread the OM headlines. The trade area is the strongest in this portfolio group: $112,238 3-mile average household income, a 5-mile population up 64% since 2010 and still growing 3.47% a year, with roughly 1,000 residential units built or proposed within two miles. The catch is that a center marketed as stabilized is really a three-year leasing project: nearly 40% of GLA rolls in 2028 and 66% is rolled by the end of 2029, none of it with disclosed options, and the 100% occupancy figure itself depends on four renewals — Omelet Cafe, Sally Beauty, Sport Clips and GameStop — that CBRE has modeled but the OM does not state as executed. Two live sales kickouts sit inside the first two years, on Bealls Outlet (the largest tenant, if February 2027 to January 2028 sales miss $2 million) and Petsense (if 6th-lease-year sales miss $700,000), together covering 17% of base rent, and no sales are disclosed for either. Add 25% of the GLA recovering zero expenses and a $0.65/SF unreassessed tax line, and the expense side carries real downside. The thesis is sound — a dominant, below-market center in a booming Savannah suburb — but it should be priced as a value-add re-leasing story with unquantified kickout risk, not as stabilized income.

keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9) — what the $1,186,779 in-place NOI, the $492,688 recovery line and the $1,811,007 effective gross revenue tie to. Where a suite has a 2027 step the PSF is the CY2027 blend; the site plan's current rate is recorded in each tenant's rentSchedule.

The OM's In-Place Pro-Forma prints lease dates as month-year only with no day. Commencements are recorded as the FIRST day and expirations as the LAST day of the printed month — a stated convention, not a figure read off the document. Re-key exact days from the rent roll.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) 119,902 SF occupied + 36,932 SF vacant = 156,834 SF GLA; (b) 119,902 / 156,834 = 76.5% occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $1,318,321 vs the $1,318,319 printed (rounding); (d) $1,811,007 EGR - $624,228 OpEx = $1,186,779 NOI. Tenant recoveries sum to $492,688 exactly.

TWO ROSTER ROWS CARRY RENT BUT NO SQUARE FOOTAGE: the Planet Fitness NNN ground lease ($50,000/yr, tenant owns the building) and the Wells Fargo ATM ($20,631/yr). Both are income-producing leases whose rent is inside the OM's $1,318,319 base-rent total, so they are carried as ORDINARY tenants rather than NAP — marking them NAP would drop $70,631 of real rent out of the roll-up and break the tie-out. They contribute no GLA. As a result the $11.00/SF weighted-average base rent includes their rent over the 119,902 SF occupied denominator, which is exactly how CBRE computes it (page 10 shows $11.01 for CY2027).

GOLDEN CORRAL IS NAP — a shadow outparcel under an REA that pays no base rent and contributes a FIXED $3,000/year to CAM. Marked NAP so it does not distort GLA, occupancy or rent math; its $3,000 remains inside the $492,688 recovery line.

THE WELLS FARGO ATM LEASE EXPIRED IN DECEMBER 2026 — before the analysis period begins. Its entire $20,631 of CY2027 rent rests on a 5-year renewal CBRE has MODELED but the OM does not state as executed.

1942 SOCIAL APPEARS ON TWO ROWS AND THAT IS CORRECT, NOT A DUPLICATE: suite 16 (3,535 SF, in place since April 2022) plus suite 14 (2,450 SF, an EXPANSION commencing January 2027), both coterminous in July 2037. Combined the tenant occupies 5,985 SF at $99,750 of base rent. The suite 14 rent is entirely forward-looking — confirm the space is delivered and the tenant is open and paying.

OLLIE'S AND CITI TRENDS BOTH HAVE 'SUBSIDIZED NNNs' per the OM highlights. Their modeled recoveries ($3.23/SF and $3.90/SF) sit below the center's $4.52/SF shop rate, so ownership absorbs part of the expense load on 23% of the GLA. Confirm the cap/subsidy structures against the leases before underwriting the recovery ratio.

OPTION TERMS vs ROSTER EXPIRIES: the rent roll shows Ollie's expiring August 2031, but the OM highlights say the Ollie's lease 'fully terms out in August 2036' — i.e. options extend beyond the roll's current-term date. Citi Trends is the opposite: the roll shows November 2031 and the OM confirms the lease FULLY TERMS OUT then, with nothing remaining. WALT here is computed off the roster's current-term expiries, so Ollie's contributes its 2031 date; the option-inclusive term is longer. The OM prints no option counts, lengths or rents — pull the leases.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $1,186,779 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED. The $260,406 CY2027 tax line is the 2026 budget grown forward; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. At $1.66/SF this is by far the heaviest tax load in this portfolio group and is 22% of NOI — Henry County, GA reassessment on sale is a first-order underwriting item here.
The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, or any co-tenancy or exclusive-use clause. Left null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: 23.5% VACANT — 36,932 SF — and 35,882 SF of it sits in TWO EMPTY ANCHOR BOXES (15,730 SF and 20,152 SF). CBRE models both absorbed in a single event on 1/1/2028 at $14.00/SF with $40.00/SF of new tenant improvements and 9 months of downtime, and the CY2028 capital line carries $1,218,422 of TI plus $317,917 of leasing commissions — over $1.5 million of capital in one year. NOI more than doubling from $1,185,016 to $1,834,060 between 2027 and 2028 depends entirely on leasing two junior-anchor boxes on schedule. That is the whole deal, and it is not a modest lease-up assumption.

GOODWILL'S TENANT HEALTH IS ALARMING: $59 PSF of sales against a 23% occupancy cost (OM-stated) on 36,015 SF — 23% of GLA and 26% of base rent — the worst health ratio disclosed anywhere in this portfolio group. The lease was just renewed for 10 years to July 2036, which reads as strength, but a 23% occupancy cost is not sustainable on conventional retail economics, and the lease is with a regional Goodwill affiliate rather than a national credit, with no guaranty disclosed. A signed term does not protect against a tenant that cannot pay.

Citi Trends' lease FULLY TERMS OUT in late 2031 with no remaining options, on 11,000 SF at a 10% occupancy cost with $147 PSF of sales. The OM presents its $11.00/SF as mark-to-market upside; at a 10% occupancy cost the sales do not obviously support a materially higher rent. Treat the 2031 expiry as a re-leasing event, not a rent-increase event.

NO SALES DISCLOSED FOR NORTHERN TOOL — the center's largest single base rent at $355,631 (27% of total) on 18.7% of GLA, expiring October 2032. The three anchors with disclosed sales run at 4%, 10% and 23% occupancy costs, so the absence of data on the biggest rent payer is a material gap.

Taxes are $260,406, $1.66/SF, 22% of in-place NOI — the heaviest tax load in this portfolio group — and expressly NOT reassessed. A Henry County reassessment to a market purchase price is a first-order risk, made worse by the subsidized recovery structures on Ollie's and Citi Trends.

Recovery leakage on 23% of the GLA: Ollie's and Citi Trends both have 'subsidized NNNs' recovering below the center's shop rate, so ownership absorbs part of the expense load — including part of any tax step-up.
The Wells Fargo ATM lease expired in December 2026 and its $20,631 of CY2027 rent is a modeled, unexecuted renewal.

Population growth is weak despite the Atlanta MSA address: 3-mile population growing just 0.70% annually since 2020 and a projected 0.62% over the next five years, with 3-mile average household income of $87,035. The '16% since 2010' figure the OM headlines is a 7-mile number over 15 years, not current momentum. The 1,450-unit Aston Wright development is planned, not built.
Two of eleven shop suites are consumer-lending operators (Heights Finance, Security Finance) and one is a tobacco/vape store — a shop mix with above-average regulatory and headline risk.

deals.notes: Freeway Junction is a 156,834 SF community center on 18.7 acres at the I-675 / SR-138 interchange (98,900 VPD) in Stockbridge, Georgia, 0.8 miles from I-75 and 15 miles southeast of downtown Atlanta, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 76.5% leased and produces $1,186,779 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $1,811,007 of effective gross revenue against $624,228 of operating expenses, at a $11.00/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $15.74/SF modeled market rent. The anchor lineup is Goodwill (36,015 SF), Northern Tool & Equipment (29,270 SF), Ollie's Bargain Outlet (25,575 SF), Citi Trends (11,000 SF) and a Planet Fitness NNN ground lease running to 2040; every anchor has been in place at least twelve years, three have recently recommitted, and all sit an average nine miles from their nearest same-store location. The entire investment case is the 36,932 SF of vacancy — 35,882 SF of which is two empty junior-anchor boxes — which CBRE models absorbed on a single date in 2028 at $14.00/SF, taking NOI from $1.19 million to $1.83 million and requiring more than $1.5 million of tenant improvements and commissions in that one year. That is a genuine value-add opportunity in a strong-access location, but it is a leasing and capital project, not a stabilization assumption. Two things temper the story. Goodwill, the largest tenant at 23% of GLA and 26% of base rent, shows $59 PSF of sales against a 23% occupancy cost — the worst tenant health in this portfolio group — despite having just signed a ten-year renewal with a regional affiliate and no disclosed guaranty. And the tax line, $260,406 or $1.66/SF, is 22% of NOI and expressly not reassessed, with Ollie's and Citi Trends both on subsidized recovery structures that leave ownership absorbing part of any step-up on 23% of the GLA. The optionality is unusually good — a separately saleable Planet Fitness ground lease, a 6.15 per 1,000 SF parking field flagged for pad activation, and deep locked-in rent spreads on Ollie's — but underwrite the two anchor boxes and the Goodwill credit before the CAGR.
